scope: Substantive refresh of a 900 word post at its existing URL

observations.summary: Removed claims that salt-free conditioners have a resin tank and a low-salt discharge that is safe for septic systems, that softener sodium on municipal sewer harms the environment, an unsourced 2 to 4 hour install time, a C-42 Sanitation license cited for softener work, and Consumer Reports and Angi sources that were not used for specific facts.
observations.inference_limit: Softener installation is plumbing work; licenses remain as listed in lib/site.ts.

observations.summary: Ion exchange swaps calcium and magnesium for sodium; resin is recharged by backflushing with salt brine; about 8 mg/L sodium added per grain of hardness removed; potassium chloride needs about 10 percent more; recharge water can overload small septic systems; magnetic conditioners lack consistent performance standards.
observations.inference_limit: General extension guidance, not product specific.

observations.summary: Brine harms tank bacteria, contributes to leach field clogging and surfacing effluent; preferred options are no softener, then an exchange tank softener, then a drywell or subsurface system separate from the septic; never discharge to the ground.
County sewage disposal ordinance: discharge from water softeners, drinking water filters and other non-domestic sources shall not be discharged to the septic system.
observations.inference_limit: Applies to septic properties in Santa Cruz County; sewer homes follow their sewer provider.

observations.summary: Hours, free quotes and flat-rate pricing restated; linked services and posts exist.
observations.inference_limit: Only confirmed business facts are restated.
